thread:
Noah Kim: Hi finance — I submitted an expense for the conference shuttle on 2026-06-02. Corpcard charged GBP 72.00 but the vendor refunded GBP 12.00 later; my expense still shows full amount and the reimbursement portal expects GBP. How do we handle the partial refund + exchange rate?
Marta Lopez: Hi Noah, did the refund post back to the same card txn or as a separate credit? Screenshot of both txn lines helps.
Noah Kim: Refund appears as a separate credit on 2026-06-05 with id REF-44c. I uploaded the statement screenshot: https://files.redwood.com/receipts/shuttle_20260602_6789.png
Priya Rao: FYI: Finance policy — net charges are reimbursable. For partial refunds we require: (1) original receipt, (2) bank statement showing both charge and refund, and (3) a short explanation. We match on txn ids and convert at the card processor rate on refund date.
Noah Kim: Uploaded original invoice from vendor and added note explaining passenger count change.
FinanceBot: Reminder: To avoid duplicate reimbursement, ensure expense amount is net (charge minus refunds) and attach bank txn lines. If vendor refunded in GBP and card converted to USD at a different rate, Finance uses payment processor FX to compute final reimbursable USD.
Marta Lopez: Thanks @Noah — I see both entries. Please update the expense amount to GBP 60.00 and confirm your bank's card FX rate isn't required (we'll use processor rate).
Noah Kim: Updated amount to GBP 60.00 in the portal and added the REF-44c id in notes.
Priya Rao: All set from policy side. We'll process at the processor-converted USD amount for the refund date. Expect in next reimbursement run.
Noah Kim: Great, thanks everyone. Appreciate the clarity.
FinanceBot: Expense adjusted and queued (ID 2026-EXP-1102). Expected payout: next payroll cycle.
